conclusion: Neutral. The default punet configuration produced a denoising_score of 0.69 on a sparse trial, which is in line with the baseline range. The high_freq_MHz regime (0.9) is the strongest, low_freq_kHz (0.5) is the weakest — the model handles MHz signals well but is leaving low-frequency content on the table.
key_factor: model_type=punet with default depth=4 and kernel_size=9. No prior records to compare against, so attribution is to the architectural defaults rather than any specific tuned hyperparameter.
discovery: On the very first round, the regime breakdown already reveals a low_freq_kHz blind spot — files 0-4 score about half what files 11-19 do. This is the same pattern observed in the baseline records and confirms that frequency-band imbalance is intrinsic to the punet defaults, not noise from this particular run.
memory_update: Next round, try widening the receptive field at low frequencies. Candidate: increase kernel_size from 9 to 11 or 13, or try depth=5 to extend the receptive field downstream. Use the same trial_portion=0.05 to keep the comparison apples-to-apples.
